text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - Bunds took a beating after news of strong M3 data and business confidence in October. But dealers said they did not expect a big sell-off and that Bunds may test their highs again by end-1996. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.89, down 0.30 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts closed down, but off earlier lows plumbed after a stronger than expected rise in UK M4 money supply in October and a dip in Bunds following a robust rise in the German Ifo index. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-8/32, down 10/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures were hit by a wave of selling after stronger than expected German economic data gave traders a pretext to take some profits after the contract hit a high earlier on Wednesday. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.70, down 0.34 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bonds futures slipped back from new record highs set in early trade as weakness in overseas bond markets undermined the current wave of optimism in Italian debt markets. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.32, down 0.79 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries remained moderately lower midday, as this afternoon's five-year note auction takes center stage. Market participants are optimistic that demand for the $12.5 billion five-year notes will be higher than Tuesday's mostly disappointing two-year note sale. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-0/32, down 7/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.45 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese goverment bonds futures ended sharply down due to comments by senior government officials, who said recent rises in yen bond prices were not in line with the performance of the economy. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.75, down 0.69 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw deals in dollars, guilders, lire, marks, sterling and yen. The emerging market sector focused on the imminent launch of Russia's debut Eurobond, now mooted for up to $750 million. BFB became the first Portugese bank to launch a $100 million structured FRN that qualified as upper-tier two capital. There were also a number of sizeable mark transactions.
